mediators.why: FOSL2 is a key AP-1 component directly activated by MAPK/ERK signaling and shows strong upregulation (log2FC=1.12, d=1.38) matching TACSTD2's BRAF-like pattern. AP-1 complexes are well-established regulators of epithelial markers and cell adhesion molecules.
mediators.literature_anchor: Murphy et al. Nature Reviews Cancer 2013 - AP-1 in cancer progression

mediators.why: STAT1 shows the strongest upregulation among STATs (log2FC=1.47, d=1.58) and can be activated downstream of MAPK through interferon signaling crosstalk. STAT1 regulates epithelial differentiation genes and cell surface markers in thyroid cancer.
mediators.literature_anchor: Kimura et al. Endocr Relat Cancer 2003 - STAT signaling in thyroid

mediators.why: STAT3 is moderately upregulated (log2FC=0.49, d=1.22) and represents a key node where MAPK and cytokine signaling converge. STAT3 directly regulates epithelial cell adhesion molecules and is frequently activated in BRAF-mutant thyroid cancers.
mediators.literature_anchor: Borrello et al. Oncogene 2005 - STAT3 in thyroid transformation

mediators.why: RELA (p65 NF-κB subunit) shows consistent upregulation (log2FC=0.34, d=1.20) and is activated downstream of MAPK through multiple mechanisms. NF-κB directly regulates cell surface receptors and adhesion molecules including TACSTD family members.
mediators.literature_anchor: Karin & Ben-Neriah Nature 2000 - NF-κB in cancer

mediators.why: TEAD1 is upregulated (log2FC=0.67, d=1.14) and serves as a key Hippo pathway effector that can be modulated by MAPK signaling. TEAD factors regulate epithelial cell identity genes and surface markers in thyroid epithelial cells.
mediators.literature_anchor: Pan et al. Genes Dev 2018 - Hippo-MAPK crosstalk

claude_inference.path_summary: The BRAF V600E → MAPK → TF → TACSTD2 axis likely operates through multiple parallel transcriptional programs, with FOSL2/AP-1 and STAT1/3 representing the strongest mediators based on their expression patterns and known MAPK connectivity. These TFs coordinate to drive the epithelial differentiation program characteristic of BRAF-like thyroid cancers, with TACSTD2 serving as a key downstream effector of this epithelial identity network.
